blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — universal application of Standard Precautions with exposure-based PPE selection
stem: A nurse is caring for clients with different diagnoses in several healthcare settings. Which statement best describes when Standard Precautions apply?

options.A: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient across healthcare settings, select PPE for the anticipated exposure, and add Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated.
options.B: Apply Standard Precautions when infection history or symptoms suggest transmissible disease, and otherwise use routine hand hygiene without exposure-based PPE.
options.C: Apply Standard Precautions in inpatient and procedural settings, while outpatient care can rely on diagnosis-specific precautions unless body-fluid exposure is expected.
options.D: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient, but wear gloves, gown, and face protection for each encounter regardless of the task or anticipated exposure.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that Standard Precautions are used for all patients in all healthcare settings regardless of suspected or confirmed infectious status. Standard Precautions include hand hygiene and a risk assessment with selection of appropriate PPE based on the nature of the patient interaction and anticipated exposure to blood, body fluids, infectious material, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, or contaminated equipment. Transmission-Based Precautions are added when a documented or suspected diagnosis creates transmission risk despite Standard Precautions; they do not replace the baseline Standard Precautions. B is incorrect because Standard Precautions are not limited to patients with suspected transmissible disease. C is incorrect because the CDC core practices apply across inpatient, outpatient, and other healthcare settings. D is incorrect because PPE is selected according to task and anticipated exposure rather than requiring every listed PPE item for every patient encounter.
educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient in every healthcare setting, use hand hygiene routinely, select PPE according to anticipated exposure risk, and add Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly integrates universal Standard Precautions, exposure-based PPE selection, and addition of Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated.
option_audit.B: Plausible infection-triggered misconception; incorrect because Standard Precautions do not depend on suspected transmissible disease.
option_audit.C: Plausible setting-based misconception; incorrect because CDC Core Practices apply across inpatient and outpatient settings.
option_audit.D: Plausible over-precaution approach; incorrect because PPE is task/risk based rather than universally requiring gloves, gown, and face protection for each encounter.
